newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz Life vows no red tape on Holocaust claims.
newsitem.headline: Allianz Life vows no red tape on Holocaust claims.

text.p: German Allianz AG Holding's life insurance arm on Wednesday pledged to use minimum red tape in its handling of a U.S. lawsuit on behalf of Holocaust survivors which claims insurers cheated them of billions of dollars.

Gerhard Rupprecht, chairman of Allianz Lebenversicherungs AG, told a news conference that valid claims arising from the suit would be honoured on the basis of credibility rather than hard proof of the existence of a policy.

Should such cases emerge from an examination of its records which is to be carried out by Arthur Andersen, "We will honour our responsibilities in every case without formal legal objections .... like gaps in documents," he said.
However Rupprecht said he expected claims to be very sparse and would not require any separate financial provision in this year's accounts.

The lawsuit filed last week in the U.S. charges seven European insurers including Allianz with concealing or converting the cash value and proceeds of policies sold prior to 1946 to victims of Nazi persecution.

The insurers encouraged Europeans fearing persecution to deposit assets with them and buy insurance to safeguard their families' futures, according to the class action suit which combines the claims of an estimated 10,000 plaintiffs.
Rupprecht said Allianz Leben planned to set up telephone information lines worldwide for potential plaintiffs.
The firm said it had one million private insurance clients and 1.5 million corporate contracts in 1938.

Henning Schulte-Noelle, chairman of parent company Allianz, has said that the insurer has to hold itself accountable for its entire corporate history, including the years between 1933 and 1945, and was trying to fill in gaps in its records.

Other defendants in the case include Assicurazioni Generali S.p.A. of Trieste, Italy, A.G.F. Assurances Generales de France Vie of Paris, Riunione Adriatica Di Sicurta S.p.A. of Milan and Bavarian Reinsurance Co of Munich.
